idea.idea: Fixing the dangerous 'Don't Ask Again' setting in AI coding agents that leaks API keys on GitHub
idea.angle: Selecting automatic approval toggles in AI automation CLI tools can accidentally commit plain-text passwords to public repositories.
idea.audience_problem: Small business owners running custom python or AI automation scripts end up leaking internal passwords and API credentials online.

Safe coding habits se data secure rakho. Comment SECURE, main aapko steps DM kar dunga.
scenes.headline: Get Audit Checklist

piece.caption: How to prevent AI coding agents from leaking API keys and passwords on GitHub. When using AI tools like Claude Code to write business automation scripts, selecting options like Don't Ask Again can cause automatic commits of secret credentials to public repositories. Over 1,120 GitHub files were found exposed due to this exact issue. Before letting an AI agent run code for your shop or office, ensure auto-approval is off and confidential keys are excluded from git tracking. Have you checked if your internal automation scripts contain plain-text passwords? Comment SECURE for the safety audit steps.

claims.claim: Claude Code's Don't Ask Again setting exposed passwords in 1,122 public GitHub files.

piece.dm_text: Here is your 3-step security audit for AI automation scripts: 1. Turn off automatic approval settings like Don't Ask Again in coding agents. 2. Ensure all API keys and passwords are stored in environment variables, not plain text in code. 3. Add sensitive configuration files to .gitignore before committing code to public or shared repositories. Read full report: https://apiiro.com/blog/coding-agents-leaking-secrets-github-dont-ask-again

review.fix_instructions: The draft is strong and ready to publish. In the DM text, briefly explain in plain terms that a .gitignore file is simply a file that tells Git to hide sensitive password files from being uploaded publicly.
